name: Ahlibank
founded: 1983 (incorporated under Emiri Decree No. 40 of 1983; banking activity began 4 Aug 1984 under QCB licence RM/13/1984)
ownership_summary: QSE-listed. The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) and its wholly owned subsidiaries hold 47.56%, and Qatari firms and individuals hold the remaining 52.44% (Annual Report 2025 and H1 2026 investor presentation). No other shareholder owns more than 5%.

shareholders.holder: Qatar Investment Authority and its wholly owned subsidiaries

government_link: Yes - QIA and its wholly owned subsidiaries hold 47.56% (H1 2026 investor presentation; Annual Report 2025).
group_structure: Ahli Bank Q.P.S.C. is the QSE-listed parent and operates only in Qatar. It has three 100% subsidiaries: Ahli Brokerage Company L.L.C. (QSE brokerage, launched 2011; capital QR 50m at 31 Dec 2025 and QR 35m at 30 Jun 2026), ABQ Finance Limited (Cayman Islands, debt issuance) and ABQ Innovate L.L.C. (Qatar, consultancy services). It reports two segments: 'Retail & private banking and wealth management', and 'Corporate banking, treasury, investments and brokerage subsidiary'. Ahli United Bank's 2004 stake and management agreement, and Qatar Foundation's 2013 stake, are historical; QIA is the current anchor shareholder.

subsidiaries.name: Ahli Brokerage Company L.L.C.
subsidiaries.activity: Brokerage on the Qatar Stock Exchange (branch trading floor, phone, internet trading, VIP lounge, Reuters order routing for institutions)

footprint: Qatar only. 12 branches and 93 ATMs (Annual Report 2025 and Overview page). The QCB licence for 2026 lists 11 type-B branches, 1 type-C branch and 91 ATMs. A new branch opened at Doha Oasis in Jan 2026.
customer_segments: Retail (mass), Premium Banking (affluent; branch Premium Lounges), Private Banking (HNW individuals, families, trusts and private businesses resident in Qatar), corporate, institutional and government-related clients, SMEs, and brokerage clients through Ahli Brokerage.
business_lines: Corporate Banking (QAR 35.0bn assets in 2025); Retail Banking (QAR 4.6bn assets and QAR 12.6bn liabilities in 2025; savings including the Winner prize account, cards, loans, bancassurance with MetLife); Private Banking & Wealth Management (QAR 2.3bn assets and QAR 5.6bn liabilities in 2025; bonds, local equities through Ahli Brokerage, structured and alternative products, a partnership with an unnamed international investment bank, and a digital trading platform rolled out in 2025); Treasury & International Banking (ALM, money market, FX, correspondent banking, EMTN and QAR MTN issuance); and brokerage through Ahli Brokerage.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Ahlibank runs a conventional Private Banking & Wealth Management division, headed by Ahmad Abukhalil according to the 2025 org chart, within the business sector led by Senior Chief Business Officer Othman Hijazi. It serves HNW individuals, families, trusts and private businesses resident in Qatar. RMs are supported by portfolio analysts. Products are local and international bonds (trading, sales and execution from AAA to non-investment grade) and QSE equities through the 100% subsidiary Ahli Brokerage. The 2025 annual report adds structured solutions and alternative assets, advisory and access to global investments through a partnership with an unnamed 'leading international investment bank', and a newly rolled-out digital trading platform for real-time market access. In 2025 Private Banking grew liabilities 22.2% to QR 5.6bn and assets 16.3% to QR 2.3bn. Premium Banking (affluent) offers RMs, branch Premium Lounges and 'investment management'. Retail investment is limited to MetLife unit-linked plans such as International Wealth Builder (180+ funds). No AUM, asset manager or in-app investing in the bank's mobile app was found.

private_banking.detail: Dedicated RMs supported by portfolio analysts, offering 'discreet personal asset and liability management', banking solutions and investment solutions. The division reported QR 2.3bn assets and QR 5.6bn liabilities in 2025, and is expanding investment, structured and alternative products through a partnership with an unnamed international investment bank.

asset_management.detail: No asset management subsidiary, proprietary funds or AUM figure was found in the group structure (S3) or on the website.

brokerage.detail: Ahli Brokerage Company L.L.C. (100%; licensed QSE brokerage launched 2011). It offers QSE access through a branch trading floor (Ahli Bank Building, Salwa Road), phone trading, an Internet Trading System, a VIP Trading Lounge for HNWIs, and Reuters order routing for foreign institutional brokers. It has its own mobile app ('Ahli Brokerage Co'). Qatar market only.

digital_investing.detail: Investing is through Ahli Brokerage's Internet Trading System and app (QSE equities only). For Private Banking, the AR 2025 reports 'the rollout of its digital trading platform' giving real-time market access; the platform and provider are not named. No investing in the Ahlibank personal mobile app was found. Retail and corporate digital platforms are being rebuilt; a new corporate platform from an unnamed 'leading provider' was due by mid-2026.

advisory.detail: Private Banking gives 'appropriate and sensitive advice' with portfolio-analyst support, plus advisory and global investment access through an international investment bank partnership. Premium Banking RMs cover 'account and investment management needs'.

discretionary.detail: No discretionary mandate offering was found on the Private Banking pages or in the AR 2025.

funds_platform.detail: The 2025 segment note says Private Banking serves HNWIs with 'investment products, funds, credit facilities, trusts, and alternative investments', but no fund shelf or provider is named. Retail customers can reach 180+ funds only inside MetLife unit-linked plans (International Wealth Builder).

structured_products.detail: The AR 2025 says Private Banking is expanding 'investment products, structured solutions and alternative assets'. No issuers or terms are published.

private_markets.detail: 'Alternative investments' and 'alternative assets' appear in the segment note and the AR narrative, with no named products.

islamic_wealth.detail: Conventional bank; no Shari'a-compliant wealth products found.

partners.what: Private Banking advisory and access to global investment opportunities (AR 2025: 'building on its partnership')
Bancassurance, including the International Wealth Builder unit-linked investment plan (180+ funds, myMetLife platform), distributed by Ahlibank on MetLife's behalf
MoU on fintech innovation and digital transformation, including use of the QFC Digital Assets Lab for tokenisation use cases (search snippet; the page could not be opened)

initiatives.what: H1 2026 results: the CEO says the bank continued to invest in digital banking, with a retail focus on digitalisation and distribution channels.
MoU with QFC on fintech, digital transformation and digital-asset/tokenisation use cases (search result only).
New branch opened at Doha Oasis.

Enterprise-wide Transformation Program with three pillars: next-generation client channels (new corporate digital platform due mid-2026; retail digital platform revamp), automation, and data/AI. Private Banking rolled out a digital trading platform.
Issued Qatar's first QAR-denominated MTN listed on QSE (QAR 500m, 3 years) and a USD 500m 5-year EMTN bond.

opportunities: Private Banking is growing fast (liabilities +22.2% to QR 5.6bn in 2025), but the published shelf is thin (bonds, QSE equities through Ahli Brokerage), and the AR describes expanding investment, structured and alternative products (S4, S9).
Bank-wide Transformation Program (2025) to rebuild retail digital channels 'benchmarking ... against leading global digital banking platforms'. Investing in the personal app was not found (S4, S19).
The Premium (affluent) tier advertises 'investment management' with no named products; retail investment is only through MetLife unit-linked plans (S10, S11).
Brokerage is limited to QSE equities; there is no international equities or funds platform (S15).
barriers: Private Banking already relies on an unnamed international investment bank for advisory and global access, and on its own digital trading platform rolled out in 2025 (S4).
Small bank: 432 employees and 12 branches; the wealth division head is not on the public leadership page (S4, S1).
Fee income is falling: net fees were QAR 69m in H1 2026, against QAR 123m in H1 2025 (S2).

discrepancies.detail: The FY2024 Corporate Governance Report (S21, Feb 2025) lists a Chief Private Banking Officer, a Chief Retail Banking Officer (Abdulaziz Al-Khater), a Chief Operations & Information Technology Officer (Izzidin Abusalameh), a Head of Retail Banking (Ahmed ElShazly), a Head of Information Technology (Rakesh Chouhan), a Head of Digital Transaction Banking (Nizar El-Jechi) and a vacant Head of Strategy. The AR 2025 (S4, structure 2025) shows Othman Hijazi as Senior Chief Business Officer, Al-Khater as Chief Special Projects Officer, Yazan Nusairat as acting COO, Sanjay Macmado as acting Head of IT, Shadi Khoury as Head of Retail Banking, Mahesh Sangisetti as Head of Transaction Banking & Transformation and Rajesh Srinivasan as Head of Strategy. LinkedIn search results (not opened) still show some earlier titles, e.g. Head of Retail Banking and Chief Retail Banking Officer.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the AR 2025 and the website. The 2024 office-holders who no longer appear (ElShazly, Chouhan, Abusalameh, El-Jechi in his earlier post) were not added; their departure dates are not published.

discrepancies.field: Ahmad Abukhalil - name and title variants
discrepancies.detail: FY2024 report: 'Ahmed Zuhdi Abu Khalil, Chief Private Banking Officer' (org chart: Chief Private Banking & Wealth Management Officer, 'Ahmad Abukhalil'); AR 2025 org chart: 'Head of Private Banking & Wealth Management, Ahmad Abukhalil' (Arabic: احمد زهدي ابوخليل); LinkedIn: 'Ahmed Abu Khalil'.
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as one person in the same private-banking post (same Arabic name including 'Zuhdi'); the file keeps the AR 2025 spelling.

discrepancies.detail: The 2 Jul 2020 release says 'Bachelor's degree in Finance and Banking'; the AR 2025 and FY2024 report say 'bachelor's degree in financial sciences'. No institution is given.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the 2020 release wording with the AR variant noted; institution unresolved.

discrepancies.detail: AR 2025 gives private assets 2005-2007 and Ahli United Bank Group Kuwait 2017-2022; the FY2024 report gives private assets 2005-2007 and 2017-2019, which overlaps the Kuwait years.
The AR 2025 classes the Chairman as non-independent, non-executive; the 2 Jul 2020 release calls him 'Chairman & Managing Director'.
discrepancies.resolution: Title 'Chairman' used (website and AR 2025); the managing-director styling is noted in appointed_note.

open_items: Q3 2026 (30 Sep 2026) results not yet on QSE: the API returned 404 for ABQK 2026-09-30 on 12 Oct 2026.

Heads of retail (Shadi Khoury), strategy (Rajesh Srinivasan), transaction banking & transformation (Mahesh Sangisetti), IT (Sanjay Macmado, Acting) and Ahli Brokerage's General Manager (Samer Totah) are confirmed only by the AR 2025 organisation chart ('Structure 2025') or the Ahli Brokerage page. None is on the website leadership roster and no biography, appointment date or 2026-dated source was found (status 'Requires verification'). Ahmad Abukhalil (private banking) has a FY2024 report biography and a LinkedIn match but is also absent from the website roster, so he stays 'Requires verification' until the bank confirms.
The international investment bank partner and the Private Banking digital trading platform are not named anywhere public.
The QFC MoU (24 May 2026) was seen only in a search snippet. The QFC page returned 404 and the release is not on Ahlibank's news list, so the counterparty identity needs confirmation.
Ahli Brokerage management page may be stale (2014 copyright). No brokerage volumes or client numbers were found.

LinkedIn (checked 2026-10-13, role-based searches only): matched Ahmad Abukhalil (S28, S30) and Abdulaziz Al-Khater (S29). No profile URL surfaced for CEO Hassan AlEfrangi (posts only) or for the retail, strategy, transformation and IT heads. Leads not recorded because the result shows no title or no employer: Othman Hijazi (https://bh.linkedin.com/in/othman-hijazi-20a7514), Samer Totah (https://www.linkedin.com/in/samer-totah-9054542/), 'Derek Kwok - Qatar' (https://www.linkedin.com/in/derek-kwok-4866031/). Other people not checked. Two LinkedIn company pages exist: ahli-bank-qsc (linked by the website) and ahlibankqatar (search results).
Premium and Private Banking eligibility thresholds are not published.

Leadership page biographies load dynamically and were not captured; biographies come from the AR 2025 (S4) and the FY2024 governance report (S21). Education, career and dates are not published for Khoury, Srinivasan, Sangisetti, Macmado and Totah; appointment dates are not published for Hijazi, Kwok, Abukhalil or Nusairat's acting role.

LinkedIn search results (not opened) still show earlier titles that the official documents have superseded: Head of Retail Banking (since 2016), Head of IT, and Chief Retail Banking Officer. A social-media post seen in search results names a 'Head of Digital Innovation' (Ala'aldin Alzu'bi) who is on no official source; verify before use.

Board: only the Chairman is profiled in this file. The 2026-2028 Board elected on 30 Mar 2026 (S23, S24, S1) also has Vice Chairman Sheikh Jassim Bin Mohammed Bin Hamad Al-Thani and nine directors (QIA appointees Akbar Abbas Al Baker, Ghanim Khalifa Alattiya and Mohammed Fahad Al-Khulaifi, the last still subject to QCB approval at the AGM; the nominee list S24 names Ali Ahmed Al Kuwari as the third QIA appointee instead). Website senior managers not in the file: Sara Ahmed Fakhroo (Head of Human Resources), Johny AlKhoury (General Counsel and Board Secretary), Maher Barakat (Chief Internal Audit Officer), Khaldoun Al-Khateeb (Chief Compliance Officer).

The Business Year interview with the CEO (thebusinessyear.com, 2026) answered 403 to the page reader (bot protection) and was not used. Searches for 2025-2026 appointment or departure news (English and Arabic) found no change at CEO, deputy or business-head level; the newsroom list for Jan 2025-14 Sep 2026 has none (S26). The Qatar Stock Exchange disclosure database was not searchable through the tools available, so a disclosure of a 2025 senior appointment (e.g. Hijazi) could not be ruled in or out.
